papers.title_in_file: Quantum Kernel Alignment with Stochastic Gradient Descent
papers.what_it_is: IBM and EPFL paper extending the Pegasos stochastic-gradient SVM solver to train a quantum SVM and align its kernel parameters at the same time.

assertions.value: The authors state that using Pegasos it is possible to train the support vector machine and align the quantum kernel simultaneously, unlike earlier work that trains a QSVM inside an outer optimization loop.
quotes: we show that using Pegasos it is possible to simultaneously train the support vector machine and align the kernel
Unlike previous work which performs kernel alignment by training a QSVM within an outer optimization loop
assertions.certainty_reason: Author claim supported by two small experiments in the same paper.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the covariant data set of an earlier work, Pegasos kernel alignment reached 100% accuracy in a 10-qubit statevector simulation using Qiskit.
quotes: Figure 3 shows that we are able to reach 100% accuracy.
using statevector simulation on 10 qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: One simulated experiment on a constructed data set.
assertions.reader_inference: The data set is built so that one ideal parameter makes it linearly separable, so this shows the method finds that parameter, not a gain on a natural data set.

assertions.value: The authors report a hardware experiment on a 7-qubit IBM device (ibm nairobi) in which Pegasos tracked a time-varying structure parameter and classified newly sampled points with accuracy over 90%.
quotes: classifying the newly sampled points correctly with an accuracy over 90%.
Experiment on 7-qubit device ibm nairobi
assertions.certainty_reason: Single hardware run on a constructed data set.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum kernels can suffer exponential concentration and flat training landscapes, and that quantum kernels therefore have to be designed carefully to allow efficient trainability.
quotes: they also suffer from disadvantages such as exponential concentration
We can, therefore, conclude that quantum kernels have to be designed very carefully to allow for efficient trainability.
assertions.certainty_reason: Limitation attributed to cited work, not shown in this paper.

papers.title_in_file: Conditional Born machine for Monte Carlo event generation
papers.what_it_is: CERN paper that trains quantum circuit Born machines to generate muonic force carrier Monte Carlo events, with multivariate and conditional extensions, on simulators and IBM hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that Born machines can reproduce the marginal distributions and correlations of Monte Carlo data sets, calling this empirical evidence.
quotes: Empirical evidence suggests that Born machines can reproduce the marginal distributions and correlations of data sets from Monte Carlo simulations.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on one physics data set at small qubit counts.

assertions.value: The authors report that conditional QCBMs interpolated to a held-out initial muon energy with good performance, and that hardware results were similar on training and testing bins, which they say suggests the QCBM can interpolate but is strongly affected by the noise.
quotes: All models achieve good performance for the interpolation.
suggesting that the QCBM can interpolate but is strongly affected by the noise
assertions.certainty_reason: Single study, small circuits.

assertions.value: The authors report that increasing the number of qubits to five or six in the one-dimensional case, or adding features in the multivariate case, made the ratio between generated and target samples per bin deteriorate even when the loss converged.
quotes: causes the ratio between the generated and target samples for each bin to deteriorate
even if the loss function converged after a hundred epochs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limitation from the authors own experiments.
assertions.reader_inference: The authors suggest the MMD loss may be unsuitable for large-scale QCBMs; barren plateaus were not observed.

assertions.value: The authors state that their proposed circuit design needs only linear connectivity and can be mapped to an IBM Quantum chip without SWAP gates.
quotes: to map the multivariate Born machine from Fig. 2, with the (linear, 1) choice to an IBM Quantum chip without using any SWAP gates.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own circuit design.

papers.title_in_file: The role of entanglement for enhancing the efficiency of quantum kernels towards classification
papers.version_note: The file name carries the v1 title (A Comparative Study of Classical and Quantum Machine Learning Models); the file read is arXiv v2 (1 Apr 2023) with the record's title. Same arXiv id 2209.05142, so the same paper.
papers.what_it_is: Paper proposing a fully entangled quantum kernel circuit for IMDb sentiment classification and comparing it with other quantum circuits and classical models.

assertions.value: The authors report that, for five features with 10-fold cross validation on IMDb reviews, their proposed fully entangled circuit outperformed classical SVM, the IQP circuit, the Hamiltonian circuit and the other classical models on all evaluation metrics.
quotes: For five features with 10-fold cross validation, we found the fully entangled proposed circuit to be the most efficient in analysing the IMDb data
outperforms classical support vector machine, IQP circuit and Hamiltonian circuit
assertions.certainty_reason: Single study on one data set; the quantum runs used a random subset of 150 samples.
assertions.reader_inference: The subset is small and the kernel circuits were run on a five-qubit device, so the margin may not hold at scale.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum kernel evaluation used a five-qubit IBM quantum computer with a random subset of 150 samples and 10-fold stratified cross-validation.
quotes: we first use a five-qubit IBM quantum computer
we perform our computation with a random subset of the data with 150 samples
we use 10-fold which samples the dataset 10-times into train and test data points.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that for linearly entangled circuits the classical SVM exceeded all linearly entangled quantum circuits in accuracy, precision and recall, and that efficiency of linearly entangled circuits decreased with more features.
quotes: the Classical SVM exceeds in accuracy, precision and recall in comparison to all linearly entangled circuits and classical algorithms
for linear entanglement, the efficiency of quantum circuits decrease with increasing number of features
assertions.certainty_reason: Result of one study on one data set.

papers.title_in_file: Semisupervised Anomaly Detection using Support Vector Regression with Quantum Kernel
papers.what_it_is: Fraunhofer AISEC paper that scores anomalies by the reconstruction loss of a support vector regression with a quantum kernel, benchmarked on 11 data sets including credit card fraud.

assertions.value: The authors report that, with simulated quantum kernels, their QSVR achieved a mean AUC of 0.77, the highest of all models, closely followed by the classical RBF SVR at 0.76, with the classical autoencoder at 0.71 and the quantum autoencoder at 0.51.
quotes: With a value of 0.77 our QSVR achieved the highest mean AUC of all models, closely followed by CSVR with 0.76.
CAE scoring a mean AUC of 0.71 and the QAE 0.51
assertions.certainty_reason: Benchmark on 11 data sets, quantum models simulated.
assertions.reader_inference: A 0.01 gap in mean AUC over 11 data sets is within what noise could produce; the authors call it slight.

assertions.value: The authors report that their simulated QSVR performed better than the quantum autoencoder on 9 of 11 data sets and on the same level as the classical RBF SVR.
quotes: our simulated QSVR outperformed the QAE on 9 of the 11 data sets and performed on the same level as the classical SVR with RBF kernel
assertions.certainty_reason: Single benchmark study.

assertions.value: The authors report that when the QSVR kernel was estimated on real IBM hardware for the CoverT and MNIST data sets, the AUC was 0.50 for both, meaning no advantage over random guessing.
quotes: The AUC was 0.50 for both data sets, dramatically lower than that of our simulated QSVR, meaning our model had no advantage over random guessing.
assertions.certainty_reason: Two hardware runs without error mitigation beyond sampler defaults.
assertions.reader_inference: This is a limitation the authors state themselves: the reported advantage is from simulation only.

assertions.value: The authors report that the QSVR used on average 50 of 300 nonzero parameters against 58 of 300 for the classical SVR, and conclude the quantum kernel led to easier reconstruction of the data.
quotes: For the QSVR, on average 50 out of 300 parameters were nonzero, and for the CSVR 58 out of 300.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single study; the conclusion is the authors own.

papers.title_in_file: Randomness-enhanced expressivity of quantum neural networks
papers.partial_detail: Main text and the computational cost supplement section; other supplement sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: Fudan University paper adding a trainable random single-qubit gate layer to quantum neural networks and proving it can approximate arbitrary target operators.

assertions.value: The authors state they prove that the random-layer approach can accurately approximate arbitrary target operators using Uhlmann's theorem for majorization.
quotes: We prove that our approach can accurately approximate arbitrary target operators using Uhlmann's theorem for majorization
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as proved by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors report that for image recognition a QNN without a random layer reached 69.8% average test accuracy, while one with a random layer reached 82.29% average test accuracy.
quotes: the averaged accuracy for the test dataset reaches 69.8%
the average accuracy for the test dataset is 82.29%
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation, one task.

assertions.value: The authors state that adding a random layer causes an extra computational cost proportional to the ensemble size Nr.
quotes: We remark that adding a random layer to the QNNs causes an extra computational cost proportional to Nr.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own stated limitation.

assertions.value: The authors state that their observable-learning numerical results are limited to small system sizes.
quotes: Although we are limited to small system sizes Nsys
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own stated scope.

papers.title_in_file: Efficient option pricing with unary-based photonic computing chip and generative adversarial learning
papers.partial_detail: Main text; appendix on payoff mapping skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: Photonic chip implementation of unary European option pricing with quantum amplitude estimation and an on-chip GAN that learns the asset price distribution.

assertions.value: The authors state that their photonic chip implements the unary approach to European option pricing with quantum amplitude estimation to achieve a quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo.
quotes: to achieve a quadratic speedup compared to classical Monte Carlo methods
assertions.certainty_reason: Speedup is a property of amplitude estimation; the chip demonstration is three asset values.
assertions.reader_inference: The experiment shows convergence in amplitude estimation runs on a 3-value problem, not a measured wall-clock speedup.

assertions.value: The authors state the fabricated chip supports an option pricing problem with three asset values as a proof of principle, and the GAN demonstration used a chip supporting up to 8 bins.
quotes: the fabricated photonic chip supports an option pricing problem with three asset values
we employ a chip that supports up to 8 bins
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup and scale.

assertions.value: The authors state they demonstrate on-chip training of a GAN that captures important market dynamics in real-life scenarios, bypassing the simplified assumptions of the Black-Scholes-Merton model.
quotes: we demonstrate an on-chip training of a GAN that successfully captures important market dynamics in real-life scenarios
assertions.certainty_reason: Author claim; the chip GAN was shown against log-normal and normal target distributions in Figure 5.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction and summary, definitions of copy complexity, and conclusions; derivations and appendices not read in detail (about 60 pages).
papers.what_it_is: Review and theory paper on data complexity, model complexity and the new notion of copy complexity in quantum learning.

assertions.value: The authors state they introduce copy complexity, the number of copies of a quantum state required to achieve a target accuracy, which arises from the destructive nature of quantum measurements.
quotes: it introduces the notion of copy complexity, which quantifies the number of copies of a quantum state required to achieve a target accuracy level
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own contribution.

assertions.value: The authors state that in a quantum system it is generally not possible to evaluate the training loss on several hypotheses with the same quantum data, making empirical risk minimization generally inapplicable.
quotes: it is generally not possible to evaluate the training loss simultaneously on multiple hypotheses using the same quantum data
assertions.certainty_reason: Theory framing by the authors for quantum-data settings; scope is quantum rather than classical data.

assertions.value: The authors state they deliberately omit any discussion of quantum advantage for machine learning, because most advantage results use ad-hoc data sets built to beat the best classical approach and a fair classical comparison is hard to define.
quotes: we have deliberately omitted any discussion about quantum advantage for machine learning
Most results about quantum advantage for machine learning involve ad-hoc datasets
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope, with a cited caveat on advantage results.

assertions.value: The authors state that each gradient evaluation of a quantum neural network consumes copies of the training data, so it is unlikely that quantum neural networks with many parameters use their copies efficiently.
quotes: each gradient evaluation requires the consumption of copies of the training data, so it is unlikely that quantum neural networks with many parameters make an efficient use of their copies
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors expectation stated without a proof at that point.

papers.title_in_file: A Hyperparameter Study for Quantum Kernel Methods
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, methods, results and conclusion; appendix figures skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: Fraunhofer IKS empirical study of how hyperparameters of a Hamiltonian-evolution quantum kernel affect accuracy and the geometric difference across 11 data sets.

assertions.value: The authors report that bandwidth t was the most important hyperparameter for both accuracy and geometric difference, and that the two depended on it in an opposing manner.
quotes: The most important hyperparameter for both performance metrics is bandwidth t
The GD and the accuracy were observed to depend in an opposing manner on t.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on 11 data sets.

assertions.value: The authors report that the number of Trotterization steps T had little influence and could be set to 9 or even smaller to avoid deep circuits, and that projecting (K) hindered the geometric difference without affecting accuracy.
quotes: we observed that T had little influence and could be set, for example, to T = 9 or even smaller to avoid deep circuits
the accuracy was not affected by K, but projecting appeared to hinder GD
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that their findings are specific to the size of the feature space they investigated, and that relabeled data sets showed different dependencies than real-world sets.
quotes: These findings are, however, specific to the size of the feature space
Relabeled datasets that posses labels that are more favourable to quantum learners show different dependencies and optimal values than the real world datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope and limits.
